newsitem.title: FRANCE: Hard for CGE to get closer to CLT-Messier.
newsitem.headline: Hard for CGE to get closer to CLT-Messier.

text.p: Compagnie Generale des Eaux (CGE) and Havas do not envisage "strong strategic relations with Compagnie Luxembourgeoise de Telediffusion (CLT) so long as CLT remains a 20 percent shareholder of TPS," CGE chairman Jean-Marie Messier said on Friday.
"CLT's presence in TPS (Television Par Satellite) is a brake" in developing relations between CLT and the new Havas/Generale des Eaux media structure, Messier told an analysts' meeting.

TPS is a competitor to CanalSatellite, the Canal Plus business in which Havas will become the leading shareholder as a result of a restructuring of its and CGE's media activities unveiled on Thursday.
Havas chairman Pierre Dauzier initiated talks with Belgian financier Albert Frere, the leading shareholder in CLT, to smooth out their relations, Messier said on Thursday.

Havas holds 40 percent of CLMM, with the balance controlled by Albert Frere's companies. CLMM controls Audiofina, which is a 50 percent shareholder in CLT alongside UFA, the audiovisual subsidiary of Germany's Bertelsmann.
Havas chairman Pierre Dauzier said on Thursday he hoped Audiofina would keep its 4.3 percent stake in Havas.
